item.title: Iran-Backed Houthis Hit Saudi Capital’s Airport in Damaging New Attack
item.description: Terminal 3 was hit and injuries were reported, as Yemeni militants try to cut the kingdom’s air links.

item.title: India Locks Down Heart of Capital to Thwart Voter Rights Protest
item.description: The anger over the voting lists has melded with grievances from young Indians struggling to find work.

item.title: The Nordic Formula for Prospering in a Dangerous, Fragmented World
item.description: Sweden and Denmark are pouring money into defense, tightening ties with each other and Europe—and moving beyond the U.S. It’s paying off.

item.title: Houthis Bombard Saudi Air Links in Effort to Cut Kingdom Off From Rest of World
item.description: Missile attacks on airports are spooking travelers and threatening another pillar of the kingdom’s growth.

item.title: Trump Strikes Deal With Putin for Russian Diesel
item.description: The president said Russia agreed to supply large amounts of the refined fuel, marking a major policy shift that eases U.S. pressure on Moscow in hopes of lowering fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Venezuela Wants to Return to the Days When Its Oil Fields Were Booming—With U.S. Help
item.description: Foreign investors are returning but find busted pipelines, chronic blackouts and an industry hollowed out by years of neglect.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of October 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Oil Prices Steady After Trump Appears to Rule Out Iran Strikes Before Midterms
item.description: Oil prices edged higher as traders weighed President Trump’s pledge not to attack Iran before the U.S. midterm elections against persistent shipping risks in the Persian Gulf and extensive offshore production shut-ins in the Gulf of Mexico.

item.title: China’s Next ‘Gray Zone’ Target: An Island Chain Critical to U.S. Defense of Taiwan
item.description: Chinese academics and media have laid the groundwork for Beijing to claim the Batanes Islands, where U.S. troops frequently train.

item.title: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Planned to Crash Into Israeli Airport, U.A.E. Says
item.description: The Emirati attorney general provided the first official timeline of Hamam al-Hammami’s travels before the attacker joined the Dubai airline.

item.title: U.S. Sanctions and Threatens to Dismantle International Criminal Court
item.description: The sanctions could cut the ICC off from the U.S. financial system and prohibit it from conducting transactions in dollars.

item.title: Masked Thieves in Italy Make Off With $5.6 Million of High-End Wine
item.description: The bandits used a company’s own forklifts to steal some 30,000 bottles of wine, including prized reds.

item.title: Nobel Peace Prize Goes to Navi Pillay, Mandela Lawyer Who Led Human Rights at U.N.
item.description: The South African was recognized for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

item.title: How a Binance ‘High-Value Customer’ Established a Financial Lifeline for Iran
item.description: A previously unreported Binance document reveals how an Iranian network used the crypto exchange to move money against the wishes of Western governments.

item.title: Walmart Wants Robots to Run Its Warehouses. Reality Keeps Getting in the Way.
item.description: Plus, a look inside Gaza shows how Israel’s military footprint is expanding, and we sit down with the Pentagon’s No. 2 official in his first interview on the job.

item.title: Iran and Houthis Try to Regain Upper Hand in Hormuz With Spate of New Attacks
item.description: The clashes underscore the region’s volatility and the difficulty that President Trump faces keeping a lid on its conflicts at least until after midterm elections.

item.title: A Glimpse Inside Gaza Shows How Israel’s Military Footprint Is Expanding
item.description: Israel is fortifying bases along a dividing line with Hamas as its military entrenches in the enclave.

item.title: U.S. Prosecutors Bring Torture Charge Against Nicolás Maduro
item.description: The deposed Venezuelan leader and his wife, already facing narcoterrorism and drug charges, are accused of conspiring to torture American detainees.

item.title: In Spain, Grief and Politics Mix After Death of Evicted Woman
item.description: The 87-year-old “Maricarmen” became the face of the struggle to fix Spain’s broken housing market. Her death turned her into a political martyr.

item.title: The Far-Left Mayor on the Front Line of France’s Student Protests
item.description: Bally Bagayoko has become a hero for protesters and a lightning rod for critics who say he is sowing unrest at French schools.
